candidates.title: TEA/TEOA matched catalytic readout with inert-gas, negative controls, and optional isotope follow-up
candidates.purpose: Test whether any TEA-versus-TEOA difference in CO/H2 distribution persists after tighter matching plus core controls, while limiting inference to a bounded donor comparison unless a platform-qualified substrate-associated signal is first established.
candidates.source_to_proposal: EV011 supports the competing explanation that both TEA and TEOA can function through reductive quenching and donor-radical formation. EV029 and GX011 provide transferable, non-Co evidence that TEOA can participate in catalyst- or CO2-associated adduct chemistry beyond simple donation. GX008 supports inclusion of omitted-component controls, inert-gas comparison, and 13CO2 checks in homogeneous photocatalytic CO2-reduction studies. Proposed transfer: in the researcher-stated Co(II)-bipyridine comparison platform, first establish whether a TEA/TEOA catalytic difference is reproducible under tightly matched conditions and core controls, then add one substrate-associated spectroscopic readout only if a pilot shows it is detectable and comparable in this platform. This is a proposal, not a reported Co-bpy result.

comparisons.inference: Primary single-factor comparison for reproducibility of TEA versus TEOA effects on CO/H2 and on any pilot-qualified observables. If quenching observables are similar within a pre-set repeatability bound yet catalytic outputs differ, H05 remains viable but unproven; if both catalytic and quenching observables are similar, the reported donor difference weakens.
Necessity control for cobalt-linked catalysis or cobalt-linked signal assignment under the TEOA condition; it does not isolate donor effects.
Necessity control for light-driven behavior under the TEOA condition; it bounds background product formation or donor decomposition in the dark.
Descriptive CO2-versus-inert-gas contrast for the TEOA condition that helps bound donor-dependent non-CO2 gas background; not a TEA versus TEOA causal test.
Descriptive CO2-versus-inert-gas contrast for the TEA condition that serves the same bounded purpose; not itself evidence for substrate-associated donor chemistry.
Origin-bounded follow-up for the TEOA condition if products are detectable; useful for excluding obvious non-CO2 product-origin artifacts but insufficient to prove a specific adduct mechanism.
Origin-bounded follow-up for the TEA condition if products are detectable; useful for the same bounded purpose and not itself a donor-causal mechanism test.

procedure: Prepare matched TEA and TEOA formulations by changing only donor identity, and verify identical reactor geometry, gas handling, illumination setup, sampling schedule, and product-analysis workflow before catalysis.

Run the two catalytic groups together with no-cobalt, dark, and inert-gas controls; quantify CO and H2 for all groups and collect the same quenching readout for TEA and TEOA with identical blanks and references.

Only if a pilot demonstrates a detectable and repeatable substrate-associated or intermediate-associated signal in this platform, collect that signal for both donors under the same sample state and timing window.
If catalytic products exceed the laboratory detection threshold with acceptable repeatability, repeat the two catalytic groups under 13CO2 using the same analytical workflow.
Predefine comparison rules from replicate baseline data, including assay repeatability for quenching and minimum reportable product signals, before evaluating donor differences.
measurements: CO and H2 quantified together by one unchanged analytical method across all groups
Predefined quenching observable for the platform, such as emission quenching or excited-state decay of the light-absorbing component
If pilot-qualified, one substrate-associated or intermediate-associated spectral feature collected with matched blanks and backgrounds
For optional 13CO2 groups, isotopic product assignment if detectable
Covariates affecting comparability, including pH or apparent basicity proxy, optical density, visible precipitation, and color change
Replicate-to-replicate variability and practical detection limits for each readout
candidates.supports: Support for H05 would be a reproducible TEA-versus-TEOA difference in CO/H2 distribution under the matched donor comparison that remains after cobalt, dark, and inert-gas controls validate the assay, together with quenching observables that remain similar within a predeclared repeatability window and, if available, a donor-dependent substrate-associated or intermediate-associated signal. Consistent 13CO2 product origin would strengthen interpretation but would still not by itself establish a specific adduct structure.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H05 would be that the TEA/TEOA catalytic difference disappears under stricter matching, or that any remaining catalytic difference is accompanied by clearly different quenching behavior large enough to account for it, or that CO/H2 signals are reproduced in inert-gas, no-cobalt, or dark controls in ways that undermine a cobalt-linked donor-specific interpretation.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive if quenching and downstream-sensitive observables both change together, if the substrate-associated method cannot be qualified in this platform, if products are near detection limits, if isotope follow-up is below sensitivity, or if donor substitution changes bulk medium properties enough that multiple latent factors vary despite nominal matching.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not invent concentrations or irradiation settings. Use the researcher-stated Co-bpy baseline values only if explicitly verified in the supplied material; otherwise perform a pilot to define a workable window where both donors give measurable but not overloaded product signals and where the chosen quenching assay is above background. Operationalize 'similar quenching' before the main run as no donor difference larger than the empirically determined repeatability bound from replicate baseline measurements with the same assay and sample state. Add the substrate-associated module only if the pilot shows a reproducible signal in both donor conditions without uncontrolled precipitation or severe overlap.
candidates.limitations: The card remains a staged discriminator because the supplied record does not establish a validated substrate-associated signal in the target platform. TEA and TEOA can alter several medium properties beyond donor identity, so even the primary donor contrast may combine donor, base, proton-management, and solvation effects. Inert-gas, no-cobalt, dark, and 13CO2 controls improve assignment but do not identify the exact active intermediate or prove a productive donor-catalyst adduct.

candidates.title: Symmetric cobalt-linked adduct screen
candidates.purpose: Screen whether TEA versus TEOA under matched P01 conditions gives donor-specific operando substrate-associated signals that are cobalt-dependent and CO2-origin-bounded on both donor sides, while limiting conclusions to descriptive donor-linked differences unless orthogonal assignment succeeds.
candidates.source_to_proposal: GX011 motivates a transferable possibility that TEOA can enter catalyst-associated adduct chemistry, but only in a Re system. EV004 and EV068 support operando state-sensitive measurements to compare catalyst-state changes with intermediate-related signals. EV085 warns that donor decomposition and altered active species can mimic catalyst-linked behavior, requiring no-cobalt and dark controls. EV080 and GX008 support isotopic and orthogonal assignment controls. This proposal transfers control logic and measurement strategy, not a proven Co mechanism.

comparisons.inference: Primary donor comparison. If substrate-associated observables differ while the chosen cobalt-sensitive observables remain similar, that supports donor-specific substrate/intermediate chemistry without requiring a distinct cobalt state. If both classes differ, donor effects may include cobalt speciation changes.

Tests whether TEOA-associated features require cobalt. A feature seen only with cobalt supports a catalyst-linked interpretation but does not by itself distinguish cobalt-linked from amine-linked CO2-derived structure.
TEA analogue of the cobalt-dependence test. Comparing this pair with the TEOA pair bounds whether cobalt dependence is donor-specific or general background behavior.
Tests whether TEOA features are light-dependent operating-state signals rather than dark pre-equilibria.
TEA-side analogue of the light-dependence test so the donor comparison is bounded symmetrically.
Assignment control for TEOA. A reproducible isotope-sensitive shift in a donor-specific feature supports CO2-derived character; absence of a shift weakens a CO2-derived assignment for that feature.
Assignment control for TEA. This mirrors the TEOA isotope arm so donor-specific CO2-derived assignment is bounded on both donor sides.

procedure: Prepare source-verified matched P01 samples and controls, varying only the listed factors and documenting reactor, gas handling, optical cell geometry, and background materials.

Run a pilot to preselect one cobalt-sensitive method that gives reproducible signals under the same operando configuration as IR; if none is viable, continue as an IR-only descriptive screen and narrow inference accordingly.
Collect during-reaction operando IR and the preselected cobalt-sensitive measurements for all groups with matched blanks and baseline handling.
Use the 13CO2 groups only to test assignment of selected donor-specific operando features and require agreement with cobalt-dependence or light-dependence before calling a feature catalyst-linked.

Report separate bounded conclusions for donor dependence, cobalt dependence, light dependence, and isotope sensitivity; do not infer a unique intermediate identity from one spectral feature or one method.
measurements: Operando IR features in regions plausibly associated with CO2-derived, carbonate-like, bicarbonate-like, amine-associated, or metal-associated species, interpreted only against matched no-cobalt, dark, and isotope controls.

One preselected cobalt-sensitive operando observable indicating donor-correlated changes in cobalt oxidation state or coordination environment; useful for state comparison but insufficient alone for intermediate assignment.
Feature persistence or loss in no-cobalt controls to distinguish catalyst-linked behavior from donor/background bands.
Feature persistence or loss in dark controls to distinguish operating-state signals from dark pre-equilibria.
Isotope-sensitive shifts or non-shifts in selected donor-specific features under 13CO2 to bound CO2-derived character on both donor sides.
candidates.supports: Support for H05 would be a reproducible TEA/TEOA difference in operando substrate-associated observables under matched conditions, with at least one donor-specific feature showing cobalt dependence or donor-correlated cobalt-state change and isotope behavior consistent with CO2-derived origin on the relevant donor side.
candidates.refutes: Evidence against H05 would be no reproducible donor-specific operando difference after matched controls, or donor-specific signals that are fully reproduced without cobalt and lack isotope support or cobalt-state correlation, making cobalt-linked or donor-specific CO2-adduct chemistry unnecessary.
candidates.inconclusive: Inconclusive outcomes include unresolved spectral overlap, donor-dependent background absorption, failure of the chosen cobalt-sensitive method to resolve state differences, or isotope tests too weak for assignment. Such outcomes may still justify descriptive reporting of similarities or differences without mechanistic assignment.
candidates.parameter_selection: Do not assume spectral windows, concentrations, or irradiation settings from unrelated systems. Use source-verified P01 settings if available; otherwise run a pilot with identical cell geometry, gas delivery, and background subtraction across groups. Advance a cobalt-sensitive method only if it can be collected reproducibly for both donors under the same sampling configuration; otherwise restrict the card to IR-based descriptive screening.
candidates.limitations: Direct Co-bpy evidence for TEA/TEOA adduct chemistry is absent in the supplied record. Heterogeneous background from g-C3N4 and mixed media may obscure weak bands. Even symmetric isotope controls do not cleanly distinguish amine-linked from cobalt-linked CO2-derived structures. No-cobalt controls alter the coordination environment, so they support but do not prove catalyst-linked assignment.
